thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty fired: P1 GPU MEMORY PRESSURE in pool `dedicated-gpu-eu-west-2`. 3 hosts reporting `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` / ENOMEM. Incident INC-20260314-2345. Please ack and follow runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory :rotating_light:

alina: acked, I'm on it. looking at pool metrics now.

ben: oncall here, also saw alerts. are we seeing kvcache evictions?

sanjay: yes, heavy kvcache churn. eviction rate spiked ~20x at 22:44 UTC. could be a regression from last deploy.

kai: stack traces from one host showing: ```
[2026-03-14T22:44:11Z] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation)
model_serving: failed to allocate workspace 256MB
last_prompts: long-chat-requests x 5
```

alina: nice logs. checking recent deployments... there was a quantization change rolled at 22:30 by model-team. rolling that back now for pool `p-eu2-gpu-5`.

ben: if rollback doesn't help we'll try draining the worst hosts out of rotation. can we detach long-running requests?

tanya: noticed autoscaler tried to add nodes but hit quota error: "insufficient quota for nvidia-gpu" in eu-west-2. autoscale failed to add 2 nodes. https://console.cloud/xxx (link)

ops-runner: paging note: customers in region-eu see elevated 429s and slow tails. approx 3% of requests in Hosted API returning 503/timeout across eu region.

alina: marking customer-impact: partial degradation EU. posting to status page draft.

ben: mitigation plan: 1) rollback model change 2) cordon+drain top 3 offenders 3) temporarily reduce batch size and kvcache retention via feature flags 4) escalate quota to cloud provider if needed.

sanjay: reducing kvcache retention now: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/serving --containers=server KVCACHE_MAX_ITEMS=5000` -> applied to canary.

kai: applied `--batch-size=4` to canary and restarting. we'll monitor.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: INC-20260314-2345 acknowledged by alina. responders: alina, ben.

ben: can someone paste the driver logs from host gpu-eu-12? I see a lot of `sigill` in dmesg around the crash window.

kai: dmesg snippet: ```
Mar 14 22:44:10 gpu-eu-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, Ch 00000001, Voluntary GPU reset, PID 9834, context 0x2
Mar 14 22:44:10 gpu-eu-12 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0 has fallen off the bus.
```

tanya: hmm that looks like driver hiccup combined with high memory. could be fragmentation + large allocations.

alina: can we evict the largest KV partitions? if we flush some kvcache across pool it might free transient memory.

sanjay: running `curl -XPOST https://kvcache.internal/evict?pool=dedicated-gpu-eu-west-2&percent=30` -> 30% eviction started.

ops-runner: metrics delta: GPU memory used dropped ~18% on canary hosts after eviction. 503s dropping but still above baseline.

ben: rolling out rollback across remaining hosts now. it's a config rollback, should be quick. watching OOM counts.

alina: rollback completed on 5 hosts. one host (gpu-eu-12) still showing kernel resets. reopening maintenance for that host.

kai: suggestion: temporarily divert traffic to ded-safepool-us until eu stabilizes? network latency tradeoff but keeps customer requests success higher.

tanya: we have capacity in us-safepool but need to update routing policy. doing a controlled shift of 10% to start.

incident-bot: Routing update: 10% traffic shifted off `dedicated-gpu-eu-west-2` to `dedicated-gpu-us-central-1` via smart-router rule rule-4721.

ops-runner: after shift, EU 5xx rate down to ~1% and p95 latency improved by 120ms. still monitoring.

ben: ok continuing to monitor. if we see repeated NVRM resets we should retire gpu-eu-12 from pool and reprovision. alina, take ownership for follow-up?

alina: taking ownership for incident follow-up and RCA. I'll open INC-20260314-2345-DOC and schedule postmortem. For now status: mitigated, partial customer impact, routing workaround in place.

tanya: handing off active mitigation to night oncall at 02:00 UTC. please ping if regressions.

ben: thumbs, great work. :thumbsup:

alina: final notes I'll include in the ticket: root cause suspected memory-fragmentation + new quantization runtime regression + failed autoscale due to quota. actions: revert quantization, request quota increase, add driver-level watchdog to preemptively drain hosts on repeated Xid resets.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260314-2345 marked as MONITORING. Acknowledged: alina. Assigned: oncall.

tanya: handing over. night oncall: @kai you'll have the playbook link and contact list in the ticket. good luck.

kai: got it, standing by.

alina: closing thread here, will follow up with RCA draft within 24h. thanks everyone. :heart:
